final.memo:
We have examined the bank's position as a regional wealth-management franchise specializing in services for affluent clients [D01]. While the company historically reported low credit losses [D01], the current environment has fundamentally altered our view of its short-term stability. 

The bank is currently suffering from a confidence shock, primarily driven by a heavy reliance on uninsured deposits [D01, D05]. This has forced the institution to seek a $30 billion liquidity bridge from other large banks to remain operational [D01, D07]. 

We require businesses with a durable competitive advantage and high certainty of long-term economics. The current vulnerability in the funding moat makes it impossible for us to assess the permanent earnings power of the business [D01, D05]. 

While the stock is available at a significant discount to tangible book value, we believe this price reflects a justified reaction to the risk of forced liquidation of assets [D04, D05]. We prefer to allocate our capital to more stable financial institutions within our existing portfolio that do not face similar existential liquidity risks [D08].
